name: MAX_FIELD_GRAPHEMES
reason: 14,000 is a chosen display ceiling, not a bound. It no longer applies to block messages, which runHook writes whole (hooks/lib/io.ts:67), or to the PreToolUse hook's additionalContext, which clipOutput leaves whole (hooks/lib/io.ts:35-46): Claude Code passes a block message whole and saves hook context over 10,000 characters to a file, showing the session its path and a preview, so the stop gate's verbatim-briefing message and the file trigger's records arrive uncut. It still clips every other string field a hook emits, including the additionalContext of hooks/session-start.ts:14 and hooks/user-prompt-submit.ts:20. This ceiling is the only bound on the thread listing hooks/user-prompt-submit.ts:20 emits straight through from renderThreadListing (src/cli/session-start.ts:31-40), which has no count cap or clip of its own.

name: BANNER_MAX_GRAPHEMES
reason: Declared at src/cli/session-start.ts:12 rather than imported because src/ must not depend on hooks/; the equality with the hook transport was deliberately broken when the transport rose to 14000 to fit an ordinary briefing's block message, and the invariant that actually matters is preserved and strengthened, namely that the banner clips itself first through clipWithMarker so the transport truncation is a no-op and never removes the marker (docs/plans/2026-08-28-continuity-goal-model/U7-capture.md:633).

name: HEADER_FIELD_ESCAPED_GRAPHEME_MAX
reason: Equals FORMER_HEADER_FIELD_WRITE_MAX, 500, the largest write cap the six briefing header fields carried before those caps were removed on 2026-09-14 (decision 01M2EDZAYDQZM9H42WEWKPMC9T). It is measured after escaping and applies only to the title and blocked_by of the short handle a second resume of a thread in the same session returns, which keeps its existing clip; the full briefing renderStepBriefing builds shows both whole and cuts no text.

name: SESSION_BODY_MAX
reason: Ruled by the human operator on 2026-09-09 (decision 01M24GFGJZEQE7JT4VJCRDBQS3). Across twenty-five entries, bodies ran a median of 2669 characters, largest 7814, against a cap of 8000; the largest is 98 percent of the ceiling, a sample censored by its own cap, so the observed maximum is a lower bound on demand rather than a measure of it. 32000 is four times the largest entry anyone has written.

name: SESSION_FIRST_LINE_MAX
reason: 50 entries times this 200-grapheme limit is 10,000 graphemes of first-line text, under BRIEFING_MAX_CHARS of 12,000 (commit d83408ccd7af7836cc13abb57098df71c7f332f0).

name: SESSION_FIRST_LINE_ENTRIES_MAX
reason: 50 entries times the 200-grapheme SESSION_FIRST_LINE_MAX is 10,000 graphemes of first-line text, under BRIEFING_MAX_CHARS of 12,000 (commit d83408ccd7af7836cc13abb57098df71c7f332f0).

name: RESOLUTION_PATH_MAX
reason: 4096 is a chosen ceiling on the path a caller sends, set to Linux PATH_MAX, the largest path limit of the systems Logbook runs on (macOS PATH_MAX is 1024). It is far above any record address Logbook writes, the longest being sessions/<ulid>/<ulid>.json at 67 characters, and high enough that a conflicted file with any path this machine can hold can still be settled, which is why the path pattern beside it is also kept loose (decision 01M2KK8AEJXRDY0XTXV6Z3CMY3).

name: SESSION_UNPARKED_ENTRIES_MAX
reason: Ruled by the human operator on 2026-09-11 (decision 01M27EQRZQF4R46NWA44Y10ZY0); across the twenty-four historical un-parked runs this store has carried, the largest legitimate run is 24 and the pathological one is 154; 25 refuses exactly that one run, at its 26th append, and leaves the other twenty-three alone; the margin is therefore zero, which is the known cost of the ruling; the bound is a pathology bound, not a page bound, and makes no claim to keep a briefing inside any size.

name: CONFLICT_CHANGES_SHOWN_MAX
reason: 40 is a chosen ceiling on the JSON paths listed per conflicted file in sync_ledger's conflict reply, which is a reading aid only (ruling 01M2KFB57P1EZKBQVZKN9ZMK1H) and decides nothing. A record changed on both sides normally differs in a handful of paths, so 40 shows every real case whole while a record with thousands of keys cannot push the reply past the tool-output limit on its own. Beyond it the line ends '(+N more)', and every version is still readable in full at logbook://conflict/{blob_id}.

name: BRIEFED_THREADS_MAX
reason: 100 bounds a machine-local file recording which threads one session has already been briefed on, so that a long-lived session cannot grow it without limit. It is not a correctness bound: the oldest id is dropped first, and a dropped id costs exactly one extra whole briefing on the next resume of that thread, which is the safe direction. A session would have to pick up more than a hundred distinct threads before the cap is reached at all.
